notes: Scope: the 170 C and C++ files listed for the area cpp-tests, at commit 7eddde7895. This file is the checked version of the sweep inventory. All 58 sweep entries were compared with the code, at each cited site and at the product reader. 2 entries were added and none was removed. 26 entries differ from the sweep: 19 had a wrong or missing fact, and 7 only got a more exact note (see changes). The scan found no name in these files that the sweep had missed. Role rule: read means that a test file calls getenv for the name and uses the value, or that a test file calls, at the cited line, a product function whose job is to return or check the value of that variable (dice_grant_active, early_parse_instance, get_sub_instances, system_parse_args under a Dice grant, default_mountpoint, runfile_path, book_initial_tokens, book_max_tokens, get_prompt_chunk_size, attn_stats::env_enabled, hw_attn_engagement_point, prequant_cache_root, prequant_cache_disabled, get_weights_path, resolve_weights, local_trace_config, require_no_trace_category_override, configure_system_start_date_from_env, golden_map::validate_rendered_at, load_golden_map_from_env). set_only means that the test files only set, unset, filter or pass the name. The reader is then product code, in the test process or in a child process, or a library. For those entries the notes say where the product read happens. Calls of wide product entry points are not listed as readers: pos_startup, pos_startup_host, get_devices, force_generate, tron::init_logging and make_cached_tokenizer run product start-up code inside the test binary, so every variable that this product code reads also applies to these test binaries (for example POS_1GB_PER_NUMA and POS_NR_HUGEPAGES at src/pos/driver.cpp:249-275, TRON_LOG_DIR at src/system/spdlog.cpp:76, USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER and VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS at src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:2189-2190). Children started with execv (rinzler in t/t_rinzler.cpp:281, runtron and rinzler in t/t_tron_fuse_multi_instance.cpp:221, programs started by spawn_cli) inherit the whole environment of the test process. Only launch_proxy filters it. Several test header comments say that ctest passes variables to the test (TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR, TRON_HEAP_SHADOW, TRON_BOOK_INITIAL_TOKENS, TRON_BOOK_MAX_TOKENS, TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT, TRON_DEFRAG_BOOKS_DEPTH, USE_HW_ATTN, SYSTEM_CONFIG). Those settings are in t/CMakeLists.txt, which is outside this area. Two entries rest on facts that are not in the checkout: TMPDIR (std::filesystem::temp_directory_path) and PATH (system and the shell). Both have confidence medium. The Catch2 library and libcurl (used by t_rinzler and t_rinzler_proxy for HTTP requests) may read variables of their own. Their source is not in the checkout, so none are listed. Files with no match for the search patterns (getenv, setenv, unsetenv, putenv, environ, envp, every upper-case name with a known prefix, system, popen, the exec family, temp_directory_path, and every call of a product function that reads the environment) were not read line by line. Audience choices that a reviewer may want to check: the Dice grant variables are marked operator because product start-up of rinzler and runtron reads them, although the Dice daemon sets them and a person does not; TRON_GOLDEN_TOKENS is marked operator because it configures rinzler_proxy, which the task lists as a deployed program.
